transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-27 11:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (AE), Diego (SE), Priya (SE), Samir (Head of ML), Lena (Infra), Noah (SecOps), Jules (PM)

Summary:
- Intro / qualification: Veritas is evaluating reserved GPUs for production inference, trying to decide between Redwood Dedicated vs hybrid with hosted fallback.
- Key constraints: strict data residency, KMS/HSM integration, predictable cost for bursty search workloads, 99.95% availability target for query path.

Topics:
- Workload profile and qps spikes
- Isolation and tenancy model (single-tenant vs shared hyperseg)
- Prewarm/hotpool and burst fallback strategy
- Security certs and encryption at rest/in flight
- Integration points: VPC peering, KMS, SSO/SAML

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from Redwood side, I'm Maya, AE, and with me are Diego and Priya on the SE side.
[00:10] Samir (Veritas): Hey Maya, thanks. Samir here, good to meet you all. I'll hand to Jules to kick off scope but super brief context — we've got a search ranking pipeline plus an assistant product — trying to move inference off ad-hoc k8s endpoints to something more predictable.
[00:25] Jules (PM): Yeah hi, our cost last quarter spiked when marketing pushed a campaign, so we want reserved capacity for baseline and an elastic path for spikes.
[00:35] Diego (SE): Got it. When you say spikes, can you quantify? 10x peak from baseline or more? Also what's the typical sequence length for your requests?
[00:45] Lena (Infra): Baseline is ~120 qps across regions, peaks up to 1.2k qps for short windows - about 10-15 minutes. Sequences around 512 tokens avg, some chat sessions go to 1k occasionally.
[01:00] Priya (SE): That helps a lot — so you're looking at a reserved pool sized to cover steady-state plus burst strategy. Do you have any latency SLO for the assistant versus ranking?
[01:12] Samir: Ranking is latency-sensitive, target p50 < 60ms and p95 < 150ms. Assistant can tolerate a bit more — p50 < 250ms. Cost for ranking is the main driver.
[01:24] Maya: Cool. A few clarifying things on ops: are you OK with a Dedicated pool with tenant isolation, or do you need fully private (VPC/on-prem) because of compliance?
[01:36] Noah (SecOps): We have customer data in some requests, and legal insists on KMS-backed key management and audit logs, plus SOC2 compliance. VPC peering and private subnet access are must-haves. Not sure about on-prem yet.
[01:50] Diego: Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and bring-your-own-KMS for Private deployments, and we can include HSM integrations in the Private offering. For Dedicated hosted in our cloud region we do offer VPC egress and customer-managed keys in some cases.
[02:05] Jules: So what's the difference in terms of isolation and noisy neighbor concerns? We heard conflicting things from a vendor about preemption.
[02:15] Priya: For Redwood Dedicated you can choose reserved GPU pools that are tenant-isolated (single-tenant nodes) or shared pools with logical isolation. Single-tenant removes noisy neighbor risk but costs more. We also have prewarm/hotpooling patterns to mitigate cold starts.
[02:30] Lena: If we go single-tenant, how long do nodes take to warm up? And what about burst > baseline?
[02:38] Diego: Warm up depends on model size and quant; typical prewarm for a 13B float16 model is minutes for kernels to compile, but with cached KV it's fast. Our hotpool option keeps a small number of nodes warm for immediate burst. For overflow we can route to hosted variants — that's the fallback path.
[02:55] Samir: Is routing automatic? We need deterministic failover and fallback policies for SLA purposes.
[03:02] Priya: Yes you can set routing policies: prefer dedicated variants, fallback to hosted lower-cost variants, or queue requests. For missions critical ranking you can do multi-path with circuit-breaker to avoid cascading failures.
[03:15] Jules: Any constraints on model compatibility? Our infra runs a finetuned mix of Eleuther-style and Llama forks, some quantized.
[03:25] Diego: We support most transformers, and we have a model onboarding path; quantized models are fine but we'll want the artifact and an eval run to check perf. Some forks may need small adapter code.
[03:36] Noah: On security — how do you surface audit logs? We need per-request tracing for compliance.
[03:42] Maya: We have token-level audit logs, and Console exposes per-route traces; we can stream logs to your SIEM via secure webhooks or S3 with encryption. We'll share the SOC2 + audit docs.
[03:55] Samir: Pricing — curious about how reserved billing works. Is it flat monthly for GPUs or usage-based?
[04:02] Maya: Core model is reserved (monthly commitment for GPU pools) plus per-token/throughput surcharge for burst usage on hosted fallback. We can provide scenarios: size for baseline vs size for baseline+10% burst.
[04:15] Lena: What's the billing if we reserve but don't use the whole capacity?
[04:19] Maya: Reserved is committed capacity; unused cycles are covered by the reservation cost. We often recommend a hybrid: reserve baseline capacity sized to steady-state and use a warm pool for quick bursts, plus hosted fallback for extreme spikes.
[04:34] Jules: We have to present CFO with clear cost per 1M tokens at p95 latency. Can you model that?
[04:40] Diego: Yes, we'll map your traffic histogram to token counts and show projected per-token unit cost across Dedicated vs hybrid. I'll prepare a spreadsheet.
[04:48] Samir: Any limitations on encryption keys? We might require HSM-backed keys (FIPS).
[04:54] Priya: For Private deployments we support BYOK with HSM. For Dedicated hosted in our region we support KMS with customer-managed keys; HSM is available with Private on-prem or isolated VPC with partner HSMs.
[05:05] Noah: What about disaster/region failover? If a region outage happens we need automatic failover with capacity to handle priority traffic.
[05:14] Diego: We recommend multi-region dedicated pools for critical workloads or a cross-region fallback to hosted. We can set traffic priorities per route so ranking traffic gets preemptive capacity over lower-priority assistants during failures.
[05:27] Jules: Are there integration templates? We want minimal engineering effort to switch from k8s endpoints.
[05:33] Maya: We provide quickstart SDKs, Helm charts for Private, and a migration checklist. For hosted/dedicated integration it's usually a few infra tasks: VPC peering, routing rules, and model upload.
[05:45] Samir: Operational question — how do we handle model rollouts and version pinning?
[05:50] Priya: Redwood Console supports model pinning per route, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to previous versions if we detect regressions. You can also tie rollouts to eval prompt sets.
[06:02] Lena: We might want strict traffic isolation between dev/staging/prod; can we have separate reserved pools per env?
[06:07] Diego: Yep, separate pools and RBAC scoping in Console; plus network segmentation if needed.
[06:14] Samir: Competitor question — we already ran a pilot with Replicate; they were cheaper per-request but noisy neighbor issues. How different are you?
[06:25] Maya: Replicate often runs on shared infra with limited guarantees. Our differentiation is the orchestration, fallback policies, and observability — you pay for predictable perf and SLOs.
[06:36] Jules: A bit of friction — legal asked about indemnities and data handling for hosted fallback.
[06:42] Maya: We'll include the indemnity language we typically offer and options for Private deployment if legal won't accept hosted fallback.
[06:50] Noah: One more — do you support bring-your-own-image/container for models? We have custom runtime.
[06:55] Priya: We can support containers for Private/self-host and in many Dedicated cases we can run customer images in isolated nodes; need to validate security posture before approval.
[07:06] Samir: For timeline, we're aiming for an initial pilot in 6 weeks, production in 12 weeks if everything goes well. Budget cycle closes next month.
[07:15] Maya: That timeline seems reasonable; we'll align SE deep dive and security pack delivery to match your budget cycle.
[07:22] Diego: We'll need your traffic histograms and a sample model binary to run a perf check; that will inform pool sizing and cost.
[07:30] Jules: We'll also need a documented fallback playbook — what happens when dedicated pool saturates.
[07:35] Priya: We'll draft a playbook: hotpool, priority routing, hosted fallback, and gradual shedding for low-priority routes. We'll share it after the SE deep dive.
[07:45] (brief cross-talk)
[07:48] Lena: Any quirks with KV cache and conversational sessions? We've seen cache thrash with concurrent sessions in our tests.
[07:55] Diego: We have session affinity and KV caching strategies; for high-concurrency you may want multiple smaller caches per node to avoid thrash. We'll recommend configuration based on your session distribution.
[08:10] Samir: Okay can we recap next steps?
[08:13] Maya: Sure — action items: Redwood sends pricing + SLA + security bundle; SEs run perf estimate and model mapping; Veritas provides traffic histograms and confirms HSM requirements; schedule a 60-min SE deep dive next week.
[08:26] Jules: Sounds good. Noah: I'll coordinate with legal on the indemnity wording.
[08:30] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[08:35] Samir: Thanks all.

End of transcript
